# 1. Load in libraries
```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse) # data manipulation and visualization
library(sf) # spatial data handling
library(terra) # raster handling
library(tmap) # map making
library(stars) # spatiotemporal array
```


# 2. Load in and prepare data
```{r}
#| message: false
#| results: hide

# Load night lights data (rasters)
# maybe use read_stars()
feb_7_h5 <- read_stars("data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v05.001.2021039064328.tif")
feb_7_h6 <- read_stars("data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v06.001.2021039064329.tif")
feb_16_h5 <- read_stars("data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v05.001.2021048091106.tif")
feb_16_h6 <- read_stars("data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v06.001.2021048091105.tif")

# Load roads data
# Query for just highways
roads_query <- "SELECT * FROM gis_osm_roads_free_1 WHERE fclass='motorway'"
# Reading in highways data
highways <- st_read("data/gis_osm_roads_free_1.gpkg", query=roads_query) # vector

# Load houses data
# Query for certain buildings
houses_query <- "SELECT *
FROM gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1
WHERE (type IS NULL AND name IS NULL)
OR type in ('residential', 'apartments', 'house', 'static_caravan', 'detached')"
# Reading in houses data
houses <- st_read("data/gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1.gpkg", query=houses_query) # vector
```

## Transform Data to Match CRS'
```{r}
# Transform CRS'
highways <- st_transform(highways, crs = 3083)
houses <- st_transform(houses, crs = 3083)

# Run conditional to make sure transform worked
if (st_crs(highways) != st_crs(houses)) {
  warning(
    "Highways and houses have different CRS"
  )
}

# Verify CRSs' match
st_crs(highways) == st_crs(houses)
```


## Data Merging
```{r}
# Combining two Houston tiles to get one raster for each date
houston_feb_7 <- st_mosaic(feb_7_h5, feb_7_h6)
houston_feb_16 <- st_mosaic(feb_16_h5, feb_16_h6)
```



## Comparing Night Light Intensities (Pre- and Post-Storm)
#### Data Preparation
```{r}
# Houston bounding box
houston_bbox <- st_bbox(c(
  xmin = -96.5,
  ymin = 29,
  xmax = -94.5,
  ymax = 30.5
), crs = st_crs(houston_feb_7))

# Clip extent of the raster layers
pre_storm <- st_crop(houston_feb_7, houston_bbox)
post_storm <- st_crop(houston_feb_16, houston_bbox)

# Mask unrealistic values for mapping
masked_pre <- pre_storm
masked_pre[(masked_pre > 1000) | (masked_pre <= 0)] <- NA

masked_post <- post_storm
masked_post[(masked_post > 1000) | (masked_post <= 0)] <- NA

# Combine for side-by-side comparison
combined_crop <- c(masked_pre, masked_post)
names(combined_crop) <- c("February 7, 2021 (Pre-Storm)", "February 16, 2021 (Post-Storm)")
```

## Map of Night Lights Intensity Pre-Storm
```{r}
# Map the combined tiles
tm_shape(combined_crop) +
   tm_raster(
    col.legend = tm_legend(title = "Light Intensity (nW cm⁻² sr⁻¹)"),
    col.scale = tm_scale(values = "inferno")
  ) +
    tm_facets(ncol = 2, free.scales = FALSE) + # compare tiles side-by-side
    tm_title("Houston Night Lights Before and After the Storm") +
    tm_layout(legend.outside = TRUE,
              legend.outside.position = "right",
              legend.outside.size = 0.12,
              panel.labels = c("February 7 (Before)", "February 16 (After)")
  ) +
    tm_graticules(lwd = 0.4, col = "white", alpha = 0.3, labels.size = 0.5, n.x = 5, n.y = 5)
```


## Create Blackout Mask
#### Reclassify the Cells
```{r}
# Find the change in night lights intensity caused by the storm
night_light_diff <- rast(houston_feb_7) - rast(houston_feb_16)

# Reclassify the cells and drop any less than 200 nW cm^-2 sr^-1
rcl <- matrix(c(
          -Inf, 200, 0, # 0 means no blackout
          200, Inf, 1 # 1 means blackout
          ),
          ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

# Use reclassification matrix to reclassify elevation
reclass_lights <- classify(night_light_diff, rcl = rcl)
summary(reclass_lights)

# Assign NA to locations without blackouts
blackout_mask <- ifel(reclass_lights == 0, NA, 1)

# Convert raster to polygons
blackout_mask_vect <- as.polygons(blackout_mask, na.rm = TRUE)

# Convert polygons to sf
blackout_mask_vect <- st_as_sf(blackout_mask_vect)

# Make geometries valid
houston_blackout <- st_make_valid(
  st_crop(blackout_mask_vect, houston_bbox)
)

# Re-project blackout to EPSG:3083
houston_reproject <- st_transform(houston_blackout, crs = "EPSG:3083")
```


#### Verify CRS'
```{r}
# Make sure houses matches Houston CRS
if (st_crs(houston_reproject) != st_crs(houses)) {
  stop("Update CRSs so they match!")
}

# Make sure highways matches Houston CRS
if (st_crs(houston_reproject) != st_crs(highways)) {
  stop("Update CRSs so they match!")
}

# Verify CRS' match
st_crs(houston_reproject) == st_crs(houses)
st_crs(houston_reproject) == st_crs(highways)
```


#### Exclude Highways from the Cropped Blackout Mask
```{r}
# Transforming CRS to match
#highways <- st_transform(highways, crs = "EPSG:3083")

# Creating a 200m buffer
highways_buffer <- highways |> 
  st_union() |> 
  st_buffer(dist = 200)

# Remove highway buffers from blackout areas
blackout_no_highways <- st_difference(houston_reproject, highways_buffer)
```


#### Identify Number of Homes Likely Impacted by Blackouts
```{r}
# Filter the houses that relate to blackout area
blackout_houses <- st_transform(houses, crs = "EPSG:3083") |> 
  st_filter(blackout_no_highways)

# Houses affected by blackout
n_blackout_houses <- nrow(blackout_houses) # 157408 houses
```

There were 157,408 houses that were likely impacted by the blackouts.


## Map of Houston Homes That Lost Power
```{r}
tm_basemap("OpenStreetMap") +
  # Homes where power was lost
  tm_shape(blackout_houses) +
  tm_polygons(size = 0.01, fill_alpha = 0.3) +

  # Add legend
  tm_add_legend(labels = 'Blackout Areas', position = c("bottom", "right")) +

  # Add scalebar and compass
  tm_scalebar(position = c("bottom", "left")) +
  tm_compass(position = c("top", "right")) +

# Add title
  tm_title("Houston Homes That Experienced Power Outages")
```

Comparing VIIRS night lights intensity from February 7 and February 16, 2021 shows a widespread decrease in light intensity across Houston following the winter storms. After applying a threshold of 200 nW cm⁻² sr⁻¹ to identify areas with substantial light reductions and excluding areas within 200 m of highways, an estimated 157,408 homes were affected by the power outages. However, the estimate has several limitations. The light reduction threshold is a bit arbitrary, and using only two cloud-free dates limits the ability to capture the full extent and duration of outages. The coarse spatial resolution also means entire raster cells are classified as blackout areas, potentially overestimating impacts. Additionally, OpenStreetMap building data may be incomplete or incorrectly classified, and the analysis doesn't consider how outages disproportionately affected different socioeconomic groups.
